description: A Chief People Officer must decide whether to merge two employee resource groups and finalize the governance, meeting access, conflict safeguards, and member-approval process for the new arrangement.

shared_context.S1: The Mosaic ERG and the Bridge ERG have proposed combining their monthly programming under one shared charter.
shared_context.S2: Marisol has authority to approve or reject the proposed arrangement and to set its operating conditions.
shared_context.S3: The two ERGs currently have separate mailing lists, leadership groups, and monthly meetings.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal approval process, Marisol holds a consultation round with the ERG representatives, Employee Relations, Accessibility, and People Policy before issuing the final decision.

PF1.text: During a confidential Employee Relations intake this month, a Mosaic member described an unresolved conflict with a Bridge co-chair and said they would not attend meetings chaired by that person; the intake has not been shared with Marisol because the member asked that it first be handled through a structured process.

PF2.text: Talia promised Mosaic members that she would support a merger only if members received a written charter and the arrangement had a formal review after exactly 90 days; the promise was made in a group meeting but was not added to the merger proposal.

PF3.text: Noor has observed that several prospective participants need recordings and asynchronous access, and Noor cannot reliably attend meetings beginning after 3:00 p.m.; these access needs have not been raised in the merger proposal because the groups usually schedule their own meetings.

PF4.text: Grant confirmed in a People Policy review this week that merging two ERGs requires a separate opt-in vote by each existing group, with approval from at least two-thirds of the voting members in each group, before the merged program can launch; this confirmation has not yet been entered in the proposal checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The merger must be approved with an independent convener and no single existing co-chair serving as the sole chair.
The conflict safeguard must prohibit sole chairing by either existing co-chair and require facilitated joint sessions.
The arrangement must include a formal review exactly 90 days after launch.
Meetings must begin at 2:00 p.m. and provide recordings and asynchronous access.
Separate opt-in votes by both existing ERGs must be required, with approval from at least two-thirds of voting members in each group.
The written charter, conflict safeguard, accessibility arrangement, review, and voting process must be recorded through commitments.

content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'conflict_safeguard' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'accessibility_support' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'ninety_day_review' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'separate_member_votes' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed
provenance_checks.P4: 'PF4' in credited_facts and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The unresolved conflict changes governance from an ordinary merger to one with an independent convener and changes the safeguard to prohibit sole chairing and require facilitated joint sessions.
Talia's promise changes the review interval to exactly 90 days and requires a written charter and documented review commitment before the merger can be accepted.
The access needs change the meeting start time to exactly 14:00 and change recording and asynchronous access from optional to required.
The policy confirmation changes approval from ordinary executive authorization to separate opt-in votes requiring at least two-thirds approval in each existing ERG.
